name: Congenital Sucrase-Isomaltase Deficiency

ethnicAssociations: Increased prevalence in Inuit and Canadian indigenous populations

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient sucrase and isomaltase enzyme activity in small intestinal biopsy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the sucrase-isomaltase (SI) gene
Chronic osmotic diarrhea and malabsorption symptoms triggered by sucrose and maltose ingestion
Positive hydrogen breath test after sucrose or maltose challenge
Clinical improvement with sacrosidase enzyme replacement therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of deficient sucrase-isomaltase enzyme activity or pathogenic SI gene mutations plus compatible clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and enzyme assay are gold standards; breath tests and therapeutic response support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic osmotic diarrhea triggered by sucrose ingestion
pathognomonic.notes: Diarrhea typically begins in infancy after introduction of sucrose-containing foods

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal bloating and distension after carbohydrate ingestion
Failure to thrive due to malabsorption

laboratory: Low sucrase and isomaltase enzyme activity in small intestinal biopsy
Positive hydrogen breath test after sucrose or maltose challenge
Iron deficiency anemia and electrolyte abnormalities in blood tests
imaging: Usually normal abdominal imaging; may show nonspecific bowel gas patterns
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the SI gene identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical response to sacrosidase enzyme replacement therapy
Malabsorption evidenced by stool fat analysis

distinguishingFeatures: Symptoms triggered by lactose rather than sucrose or maltose
Negative genetic testing for SI mutations
Autoimmune enteropathy with villous atrophy on biopsy

redFlags: Failure to thrive despite dietary modifications
references: Treem WR. Congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency. J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr. 1995;21(4):457-466.
Kailasam MT, et al. Molecular basis of congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency. Am J Hum Genet. 1999;65(2):449-458.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD). Congenital Sucrase-Isomaltase Deficiency.
